Patch Notes

4.3.0 — Sentinel adversarial assurance on the hardened 4.2.1 base

This release adds GUILD-039, the Sentinel Adversarial Assurance Guild, and SO-026 continuous artifact security monitoring, as an additive assurance layer on top of the fully-remediated LPOS v4.2.1 base. Sentinel does not change the security posture established by 4.2.1; it adds an independently reviewed adversarial-assurance capability over Chip-created work.

Additive assurance — what Sentinel is and is not

  • Sentinel is additive. The 14 findings from the external audit were closed by the

v4.2.1 remediation (verified-channel approvals, the hash-chained event store, the hardened dashboard and monitor, the truthful compliance readiness monitor, the always-on schema gate, and the signing/SBOM tooling). Sentinel did not close those findings, and its presence must never be represented as doing so.

  • Sentinel is not trusted because it is a security guild. Its raw scanner output

starts explicitly untrusted and must pass LPOS's ordinary fresh-context independent adversarial review plus deterministic structural verification before any finding can block work, authorize anything, or be presented to the Principal as fact.

Added

  • Constitution Article VIII: no component or new guild is trusted by designation, and no

producer may approve, certify, remediate, or close its own material output.

  • SPECIALIST-033, Adversarial Assurance Engineer, and SO-026, Continuous Adversarial

Assurance (scheduled backstop every five minutes).

  • Passive security checks on every persisted Chip artifact revision, with hash-bound

untrusted raw assessments, fresh-context independent review, and deterministic structural re-scanning.

  • Principal security reports with prioritized remediation and verification steps.

Reviewed Critical/High findings block completion of only the affected revision, and only after the assessment itself passes independent review.

  • lpos sentinel administration commands (status, scan, reports, show, ack).

Improvements over the development candidate

Two latent weaknesses in the Sentinel candidate were fixed during integration onto the hardened base:

  • Sentinel's own record tables are anchored to the tamper-evident event chain. In

addition to append-only triggers, every assessment, review, and report hash is recorded in the 4.2.1 SHA-256 hash-chained event stream, and integrity_check now reconciles the Sentinel tables against that chain. Editing a stored record after dropping its triggers — or flipping a review's trust decision — is detected.

  • **The active-engagement authorization gate goes through the 4.2.1 verified-channel

assertion path.** A fabricated MessageIdentity whose provider has no registered channel verifier cannot mint an approval grant, so it cannot authorize a Sentinel active engagement. The gate fails closed.

Counts

  • Specialists 32 → 33, Standing Operations 25 → 26, benchmarks 53 → 55, schemas 17 → 20.

Safety and scope

Sentinel is passive by default: continuous operation never executes an artifact, opens a network connection, uses credentials, invokes a shell, or changes live state. Active penetration testing requires a separately approved, isolated, time-bounded scope bound to an ordinary LPOS approved action. Sentinel is an additive defense layer, not a proof that work is secure, not a substitute for an authorized human-led penetration test, and not a SOC 2 attestation.

Hardening and governance in this release

  • LPOS-15 (audit follow-up) closed. Monitor and compliance state files are now created 0600 via the shared secure-write helpers (regression-tested under umask 022), and lpos doctor --hermes-root <root> audits state-file permissions and fails closed if any are group/other-readable — matching the coverage the 4.2.1 notes claimed.
  • OS Upgrade Radar captured (not installed). docs/OS-UPGRADE-RADAR.md records the external candidates from the 2026-07-23 architect handoff as governed design inputs behind an acceptance gate; none are installed — promotion requires its own build, audit, and Principal approval.
